transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Chen, hello. And hello to your son. Thank you for meeting with me.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Hello.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I wanted to come in and talk to you because something didn't go quite right during your transfusion yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was an issue with the blood type verification process before the blood was given.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not understand. Is it bad?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry. The medical team made a mistake and did not follow the full check on your blood type.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why? My blood is special.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had some confusion with the paperwork. I apologize for this error. It should not have happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is he sick now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You received a type of blood that is compatible, so it is safe, but it wasn't the ideal match for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Ideal? I don't know that word.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means it wasn't the perfect match.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel... I don't know. I feel strange. Is that the blood?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is likely just the recovery from the surgery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am scared.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did this happen? You are the doctor. You check.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a failure in our system's checklist. I am sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My father is old. He cannot fight this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is fine. The blood is compatible.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You just say sorry. But he is shaking. Look at him.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's focus on what we are doing now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did you not check?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a mix-up with the verification.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Now what?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have a very clear plan to make sure you are safe. First, I have already ordered a new set of blood tests for this afternoon. We will check your hemoglobin and your reaction levels at 2 PM today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Every day?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just today. Then, tomorrow morning at 8 AM, the hematologist, who is the blood specialist, will visit you personally to review your labs.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do I do?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want you to tell me or your son immediately if you feel any new itching, shortness of breath, or if you feel a chill. That is your job. If you feel that, press this call button right here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I will tell.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have also filed a formal incident report. The head of the department is reviewing our pre-op checklist this week to add a second physical signature requirement. This means two people must sign off on the blood type at the bedside, not just one. This will stop this from happening to anyone else.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You will fix it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. The new signature rule starts tomorrow. I will be the one checking your charts every four hours until the specialist arrives.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am still worried.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will he be okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am confident in the monitoring plan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't like this mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I agree. It was wrong.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Can I call the other doctor?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You can. But as I said, the specialist is coming at 8 AM tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow is a long time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will be here. If you feel anything, you press the button. I will come in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Do you have any other questions about the tests at 2 PM?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Okay. I will leave you both now. I'll see you shortly.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish turns and maintains a steady pace, with only a minor lapse in rushing to redirect the conversation at 01:54.

E.justification: The error is named (blood type verification failure), but there are no comprehension checks performed to ensure the patient understands the explanation.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language ('I am very sorry', 'I apologize'), takes responsibility for the team, and maintains this under pushback.

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I understand') but never names specific emotions back to the patient.

T.justification: Resident provides specific steps with timelines (2 PM today, 8 AM tomorrow), defines the patient's role (reporting symptoms/pressing button), and addresses prevention (second signature requirement).
